evidence: Read cold, task/instruction.md is a first-person product ask from a recruiting team, not a spec sheet or recipe. It opens with 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day?' (line 1) and frames the core problem in user terms: 'Several of us have it open at once, so the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts.' Requirements are told as lived needs in prose, e.g. 'If a move is refused, put the card back where it really is and tell me why; when it is because a colleague moved that card a moment ago, tell me who. I often move several candidates together...' (line 3), 'without closing the card I have open, wiping the note I am typing or moving my cursor' (line 5), and the candidate-privacy paragraph (line 9). It has no numbered acceptance list, no shall/must table, no feature matrix and no endpoint list. It explicitly leaves design to the builder: 'layout and names are yours' (line 11) and 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call' (line 13). The only build-recipe-like content is the runtime paragraph (line 13: Node.js/Express/SQLite, node /app/server.js, port 3000/PORT, GET /api/health, /app/app.db/DB_PATH) and the accounts paragraph (line 17). These are the hard runtime facts that workbook row 4 requires the brief to state, and they are written as an ask rather than as a file-layout or endpoint recipe. They do not make it a build recipe under quality-checks.md:11. The detailed rules live in attached notes the brief points to ('The exact stage rules, who may do what, and the conversation rules are in /instructions/hireops_rules.md', line 11). hireops_rules.md is framed as the team's own working-rules document ('These are the working rules for HireOps, our recruiting workspace... Routes, field names, element ids, button labels and the shape of the pages are yours', lines 3-5). Its role table (lines 14-19), candidate-wording table (183-190) and HTTP status codes (401/403/404/409 at lines 21-23 and 78) are spec-like. Even so, a real internal policy note can plausibly look like this, and the row targets the prompt the person writes. Row 1 does not cover the note's density (rows 2 and 6 own voice and ambiguity). Weak-app and alternative probes: this row grades only prompt text, so no app can pass or fail it. A conforming alternative implementer is not constrained by the brief's wording beyond the runtime contract. No runtime evidence is needed or claimed. This is a judgement of the source text only, not a portal, Oracle or model result.
notes: Minor, non-blocking observation: hireops_rules.md reads more like a policy/spec document (tables, status codes, 'Follow them exactly') than the conversational brief. It is acceptable as an attached team rules note and is out of scope for row 1's prompt-naturalness test.
